result.topic_en: Statements of asymptotic bounds on the fractional part of N e^{2/a} (and on its distance to the next integer) in terms of log log N / (|a| N log N), for a any integer, any even integer, and any odd integer.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94 $^{18 (16)}$ (16)
See Q. 784(ii) in volume. This goes further.

Let $[x]$ denote the greatest integer in $x$.

I a is any integer
It is possible to find an integer $N$ as large as we please such that
(1) $Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} - [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] < \frac{(1+\epsilon)\log\log N}{|a| N \log N}$
however small $\epsilon$ may be.
Given $\epsilon$, there is a $\delta$ such that
(2) $Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} - [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] > \frac{(1-\epsilon)\log\log N}{|a| N \log N}$
for all values of $N$ greater than $\delta$.

II a is any even integer
It is possible to find an integer $N$ as large as we please such that
(3) $1 + [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] - Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} < \frac{(1+\epsilon)\log\log N}{|a| N \log N}$.
Given $\epsilon$, there is a $\delta$ such that
(4) $1 + [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] - Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} > \frac{(1-\epsilon)\log\log N}{|a| N \log N}$
for all values of $N$ greater than $\delta$.

III a is any odd integer
It is possible to find $N$ as large as we please such that
(5) $1 + [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] - Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} < \frac{(1+\epsilon)\log\log N}{4|a| N \log N}$.
Given $\epsilon$, there is a $\delta$ such that
$1 + [Ne^{\frac{2}{a}}] - Ne^{\frac{2}{a}} > \frac{(1-\epsilon)\log\log N}{4|a| N \log N}$
for all values of $N$ greater than $\delta$.
